description: Fault dips measured by Wheeler Feer on HiRISE DTMs, plus programmatic HiRISE Fisher means. The explorer defaults to the Wheeler means where he measured them. Generated by scripts/convert_measured_dips.py.
upstream: Tables copied from Andrew-MSU/mars-tectonic-reactivation (private research repository), data/derived and the programmatic strike/dip note, sections 4, 7, and 8. They are committed in this public repository so the explorer's defaults can be regenerated.
caveat: These dips are surface wall and scarp slopes measured on HiRISE DTMs. They are a proxy for fault dip near the surface, not a measured fault plane at depth. Degraded walls, talus, and wrinkle-ridge flank slopes can understate the true fault dip, especially at Isidis.

sources.label: Wheeler measured (default)
sources.description: Means of Wheeler Feer's three-point HiRISE dips, by region.

sources.label: HiRISE programmatic
sources.description: Fisher means of HiRISE wall planes along his polygons or SIM 3292 traces.

fit.summary: A segment uses a measured dip direction when its strike is within 30° of that wall set and its right-hand normal is within 45° of the measured dip direction. Otherwise the dip direction stays the right-hand normal of the trace. The literature source does not substitute a measured direction.
fit.rule: Undirected strike difference to the wall set's axial mean strike must be within strike_tolerance_deg, and the directed difference between the segment's right-hand normal (strike + 90°) and the wall's dip direction must be within dip_direction_tolerance_deg. The 45° facing limit is the same cut the HiRISE wall detector used. Among walls that fit, the dip direction closest to the right-hand normal wins, so a trace is not flipped onto the opposite wall. The dip angle stays the regional slider. Individual three-point dips are not copied onto a SIM 3292 trace: the Valles Marineris sites sit tens to hundreds of kilometres off the nearest SIM tectonic line, and one wall triangle should not set a regional fault.

normal.method: Wilkins and Schultz (2003) MOLA scarp modeling. Sheet key theta_normal.
normal.summary: Literature default from the parameter sheet: 60° (slider 50–70°). Standard Andersonian extensional fault dip confirmed by MOLA topographic modeling in Valles Marineris and Cerberus Fossae (Wilkins & Schultz 2003).

thrust.method: Schultz and Watters (2001) elastic dislocation model. Sheet key theta_thrust.
thrust.summary: Literature default from the parameter sheet: 30° (slider 20–40°). Schultz & Watters (2001)

wheeler.method: Three-point plane on a HiRISE DTM triangle, right-hand rule. dip_deg is dip_3pt, the recomputed three-point solution, not the delivered Dip column. Measured by Wheeler Feer.
wheeler.summary: Mean of Wheeler Feer's four Valles Marineris three-point dips (Marineris1 36.9°, Marineris2 57.9°, Marineris3 45.9°, Marineris4 66.4°): 51.79°. The slider spans the measured minimum to maximum.

hirise.method: Fisher mean of poles to 60 m robust planes, confidence classes A and B, at stations every 200 m along Wheeler's polygon walls. The wall is the steepest 40 m Horn slope facing into the polygon. Method note section 7.
hirise.summary: HiRISE programmatic alternative for Valles Marineris normal faults: the n-weighted mean of the opposed outline-wall Fisher means, 232/27 (n=34, κ=15.41, α95=6.48°) and 336/26 (n=20, κ=17.62, α95=8.00°). The slider spans each mean ± its α95. These are generalized outline slopes and are gentler than Wheeler's mid-wall sites. SIM contact walls 205/29 (n=341, κ=16.88, α95=1.91°) and 020/28 (n=379, κ=13.82, α95=2.02°), and SIM graben-axis walls 194/21 (n=61, κ=43.32, α95=2.79°) and 016/22 (n=35, κ=68.63, α95=2.95°), are kept for dip direction when a segment is parallel to them.
